title: How many little squares are in each stacked square?
description: The little squares in the stacked squares are counted and give one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five. Each stack is n rows of n little squares, which explains the counts.
teaching_notes: One idea: a stack with n rows has n little squares in every row, so it holds n times n of them. Watch for students who add a row only and forget the new column.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (Try This), p.12
video_script.why: The child counts the little squares in each stacked square and explains the counts by what each new stack adds, using the method of the solved example on matchsticks.
video_script.substitution: Little squares in stacks are counted in place of matchsticks in a row of triangles.
video_script.anchor: a row of stacks of little squares, from one to five rows, with the count written under each
video_script.payoff_line: The little squares are the square numbers, one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five

final_answer.value: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, the square numbers; each shape is n rows of n little squares
final_answer.spoken: one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five, the square numbers

maths_rules: a stack with n rows has n little squares in each row, so n x n
check: the fourth stack plus a row of 5 and a column of 4 gives 16 + 9 = 25
video_script.design: The stacks stand in a row with the little squares counted under each. One stack is read by its rows and columns, and a new row and column are added for the check.

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, count the little squares in each stack from left to right. They are one, four, nine, sixteen and twenty five.

<bookmark mark='four'/>The fourth stack has four rows with four little squares in each.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the rule: n rows of n little squares = n x n; 2 x 2 = 4, 3 x 3 = 9, 4 x 4 = 16

marks.rule: the words n rows of n are written, and the count is written as n x n
marks.mult: the counts four, nine and sixteen are written as two times two, three times three and four times four

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, see the rule. A stack with n rows has n little squares in every row. It holds n times n of them.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Two times two is four, three times three is nine, and four times four is sixteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the fifth stack: 16 + a row of 5 and a column of 4 = 16 + 9 = 25

marks.add: a row of five and a column of four little squares are added to the fourth stack
marks.total: the nine new little squares are added to sixteen, giving twenty five, which matches five times five

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, check the fifth stack. Add a row of five and a column of four to the fourth stack.
<bookmark mark='total'/>That adds nine little squares, and sixteen plus nine is twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, the square numbers; each shape is n rows of n little squares
